meta.title: Quelio – Turn everything you read into a quiz
meta.description: Paste text, a PDF or a link and Quelio finds the key facts and turns them into quizzes, flashcards, songs and audio lessons. It also solves a photo of a math problem step by step. Free during the beta.

hero.title: Turn everything you read into a quiz.
hero.sub: Paste text, drop a PDF or share a link. Quelio finds the key facts and writes the questions, so you can test yourself.
hero.demoLabel: Example of key facts in a text turning into quiz questions

photo.name: Photosynthesis
photo.l1: Photosynthesis is how plants make food from light energy.
photo.l2: It happens in the chloroplast and uses carbon dioxide and water.
photo.l3: In the end, glucose and oxygen are formed.
photo.q1: In which part of a plant cell does photosynthesis take place?

science.l1: By Newton's first law, an object keeps its state of motion unless an outside force acts on it.

science.q1: What is the tendency of objects to keep their state of motion called?
science.q2: An object with more mass has more inertia.

vocab.name: English vocabulary
vocab.l3: scarce: hard to find, in short supply

s1.title: Paste it, drop it, or share a link
s1.body: Your class notes, a chapter from a book, a PDF or a web page will do.

s2.title: Quelio finds the key facts
s2.body: It pulls the facts out of your text first, then writes a question for each one. It won't invent facts that aren't in your text; if there isn't enough, it asks fewer questions.

s3.title: Learn with quizzes, cards, songs and audio
s3.body: One source gives you a quiz, flashcards, a song and an audio lesson. Pick whatever suits you.

features.title: One source, five ways to study
features.sub: These are examples from Quelio's real interface. Tap the tabs.

create.title: Every question type, one click
create.body: Multiple choice, true/false, matching, fill in the blank, short answer and open-ended questions. You choose the difficulty and how many.
create.mcqQ: Which gas do plants take in during photosynthesis?
create.fillQ: Plants turn light energy into {{blank}} energy.

solve.title: Snap a photo, see the solution step by step
solve.body: Upload a photo of a math problem and Quelio shows the solution with the reason for every step. You can have your own working checked, too.
solve.question: If 2x + 6 = 14, what is x?

cards.title: Learn it once, remember it for good
cards.body: Cards come straight from a quiz or a text. The ones you know show up rarely; the ones you struggle with come back sooner.
cards.tapHint: Tap the card to flip it

songs.title: Memorize a topic as a song
songs.body: The facts from your quiz questions go into the lyrics, and the lyrics are checked against your source before a song is made.
songs.l2: Water and CO2 meet in the chloroplast
songs.l3: Glucose is the food, oxygen drifts away
songs.l4: That's photosynthesis, now you won't forget

lesson.title: Put your headphones on and listen
lesson.body: Two hosts talk the topic through and ask you questions along the way. On a walk, on the bus, before bed.
lesson.hint: A short example. No sound in this language.
lesson.l1: Do plants use light energy to make food?
lesson.l3: Yes. In photosynthesis, a plant uses light energy to make food. Let's look at where it happens, what goes in, what comes out and how fast.

audiences.title: Who is it for?
audiences.sub: Whatever you study, your source is ready.

school.title: Unit tests and entrance exams
school.body: Paste your class notes or a chapter and get practice questions of your own. Stuck on a math problem? Snap a photo and see the solution step by step.

university.title: Midterm and finals week
university.body: Upload your lecture notes or slide PDF. Quelio finds the concepts and turns them into a quiz and flashcards, so you can test yourself before the exam.

exam.title: Months of revision, sorted
exam.body: Paste a history summary or a word list and turn it into cards. Spaced repetition decides when each card comes back, so you don't have to.
exam.front: In which year was the Battle of Manzikert fought?

teacher.title: A quiz ready for your class
teacher.body: Paste your lesson text and choose the question types. Print the quiz or copy it, with the answer key alongside. AI can make mistakes, so give it a quick read before you hand it out.

try.title: Try it yourself
try.sub: Pick a sample text and watch its quiz come together. This is a pre-made demo and makes no AI request.
try.cta: Try it with your own text

plans.title: Plans
plans.sub: Coming soon. For now it's a beta, and everything is free.

free.name: Free
free.desc: To get started and study regularly.
free.f1: Quizzes from text, files and links
free.f2: Step-by-step solutions for photos of math problems
free.f4: Interface in English, Turkish and Western Armenian

pro.name: Pro
pro.desc: For people who want to do more.

what.a: A study tool that uses AI to turn what you write, upload or link into quizzes, flashcards, songs and audio lessons, and solves a photo of a math problem step by step.

languages.q: Which languages does it work in?
languages.a: The interface comes in English, Turkish and Western Armenian. You can make quizzes in many more languages; you choose the output language.

free.a: Yes, it's free during the beta. Plans are coming soon, and we'll announce what they include and what they cost here.

data.a: We keep your email address, your name, and the quizzes, cards, songs and lessons you make, so they're the same on every device. The text or photo you submit is sent to AI providers to produce the content. From your account page you can download everything or delete your account along with all its data.

files.a: PDF, Word (.docx), plain text (.txt) and Markdown (.md) files, plus web page links. For math problems, a photo is enough. YouTube links aren't supported yet; paste the video's transcript instead.

teachers.a: Yes. Make a quiz for your class from your lesson text, choose the question types, then print or copy it. You can get a version with the answer key, too.

trust.a: Questions are based on the source you give; Quelio doesn't fill gaps with facts that aren't there. AI can still make mistakes, so review the questions before an important exam or before you hand them out.

phone.q: Does it work on my phone?
phone.a: Yes. It opens in your browser, so you can use the same account on a phone, tablet or computer. There's nothing to download.

cta.title: Whatever you read today, turn it into a quiz.
